text_blocks.snippet: Scammers in Central Illinois frequently target residents using fake text messages about unpaid tolls or traffic fines, imposter phone calls claiming missed court appearances, and deceptive home repair schemes.

list.snippet: Fake Toll and Traffic Text Messages: Fraudsters send text messages claiming you owe money for delinquent toll roads or traffic tickets, threatening driver's license suspension. Government agencies do not use unprompted texts for payment.
Law Enforcement Phone Imposters: Callers impersonate local sheriffs or court officials, demanding immediate payment via Bitcoin or cash to clear fake arrest warrants.

Home Repair and Storm Scams: Con artists go door-to-door or set up fake local business websites (such as bogus garage door repair or post-storm contractors) demanding large cash deposits upfront without providing valid licensing.
Do not click links: Never open unfamiliar links in unexpected text messages or emails.

Hang up immediately:
Law enforcement and courts will never call to demand money or crypto over the phone.
Verify contractors: Check for branded company vehicles, physical addresses, and official local licenses before hiring repair services.

Report fraud:
File complaints with local law enforcement or through the Federal Trade Commission. You can also contact the Office of the Illinois Attorney General consumer fraud hotline.
